transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
The Supreme Court opens a new term this week, NPR's Nina Totenberg takes a look at some
of the cases that could come before the courts.
Even as the justices will hear major cases on climate change, immigration, guns and religion,
there are many more hot button issues waiting in the wings.
Among them, whether the court will reverse nearly a half century old precedent that bars
the posting of the ten commandments in public school classrooms.
More immediately, though, the justices are likely to be drawn into the election.
The Trump administration has sought to influence elections in numerous ways, and Democrats
have lawyers across the country ready to fight what they perceive as illegal measures.
In the end, though, some of these clashes are bound to make it to the Supreme Court.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has chosen the person who will lead the investigation into
two failed executions this year, as Mariana Bacchiao at member station WPLN reports.
The governor is again tapping former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton.
Lee called for the third party review after last week's botched execution left Christa
Pike in critical condition but alive at a local hospital.
The current lethal injection process was developed after Stanton's last review found problems
with how the state inspected the drugs it uses to carry out the death penalty.
Lee says Stanton's investigation will determine if the current protocol was followed and evaluate
its effectiveness from there.
In the meantime, the governor has called off the remaining executions scheduled for this
year.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacchiao in Nashville.
The midterm elections are now less than a month away, and polling shows that chances
for a big Democratic win are climbing.
But as NPR's Domenico Montanaro tells us, a lot can still happen between now and November
3rd.
It's not election day.
Things can change no matter what.
And the fact is that everything shows movement in Democrats' direction.
When everything heads in one direction, that's important.
You know, that's all that really should be taken away from the polls at this point.
Midterms are always tough on the president's party.
The president himself has acknowledged that many times.
The national mood, especially when it comes to the economy and the war in Iran, are against
the president and his party.
High school students in France say they'll resume their protests this week over what
they say are inequalities in the school system.
They say teaching, facilities and opportunities for advancement are not as good for students
in disadvantaged neighborhoods.
France's education minister says as many as 500 schools will be closed on Monday because
of those protests.
German Chancellor Friedrich Mertz announced a new aid package for Ukraine on Sunday.
The aid is valued at more than 1.3 billion euros.
Much of that money is for military assistance, including long-range strike weapons and combat
drones.
Mertz announced the new aid during a visit to Kiev.
The visit came as Russia continues to increase its attacks on Ukrainian cities.
You're listening to NPR News.
The president of Cornell University says the institution must do better.
A former student has filed a civil lawsuit against the school, alleging she was gang-raped
at a fraternity house in 2024, MPS Kristin Wright reports.
Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff says it's a defining moment for the university.
What happened to Jane Doe in 2024 is deeply disturbing and will weigh heavily on our community
for years to come.
He acknowledges mounting questions over Cornell's handling of the young woman's rape allegations
and concerns about campus culture.
It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault.
Dehumanization and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use.
Cornell's president says the school's taking immediate action to strengthen sexual assault
prevention and education and substance use resources, and will take a serious look at
the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life.
He also announced an outside review into Cornell's handling of the case.
Kristin Wright, NPR News.
The Coast Guard has called off the search for any possible survivors from a medical transport
plane that went missing early Saturday morning off the eastern U.S. coast.
The plane was traveling from Bermuda to Boston and was carrying six people, including four
from Canada.
There was little change at the top of the AP college football rankings following Saturday's
games.
In Week 5, Texas, Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami and Ohio State hold down the top five spots.
The defending national champion Indiana fell one spot to seventh, despite beating Rutgers
47-15, while Alabama inexplicably leapfrogged Indiana to land at number six.
BYU is an eighth, while one lost Ole Miss in LSU round out to top 10.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
Support for NPR and the following message come from Washington Wise.
Decisions made in Washington can affect your portfolio every day.
Washington Wise from Charles Schwab is an original podcast that unpacks the stories making
news and how they may affect your finances and portfolio.
Host Mike Townsend and his guests explore policy initiatives for retirement savings, taxes,
trade, and more.
Download the latest episode and follow at Schwab.com/WashingtonWise or wherever you listen.

topics.text: Supreme Court begins new term with cases on climate change, immigration, guns, religion, and Ten Commandments in schools
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee names former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton to lead investigation into two failed executions
Polling shows Democratic chances for big midterm election win are climbing with less than month until November
High school students in France resume protests over inequalities in school system, 500 schools closing Monday
German Chancellor Friedrich Mertz announces 1.3 billion euro aid package for Ukraine including military weapons and drones
Cornell University president acknowledges deep concerns over handling of gang rape allegation and announces outside review
Coast Guard calls off search for medical transport plane missing off eastern U.S. coast with six people
College football rankings largely unchanged with Texas, Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami, Ohio State in top five
